content:
Fox News host Mark Levin on Tuesday appeared to have a meltdown after being locked out of his AOL email account, and rather than dealing with the matter privately, he regaled his 5 million followers on X with the ordeal — to untold mockery even from fellow conservatives.

“Folks, I have spent literally the entire day trying to get someone at AOL to unlock my email,” Levin wrote Tuesday. “For the last eight hours, I have been told that the issue has been escalated to supervisors who would contact me. I haven’t heard a thing.”

He continued, “You would think that, since I’m one of the last human beings on the face of the Earth still using AOL, they would take care of this. You’d be wrong. So, once this gets resolved, hopefully before the next presidential election, I’m dropping them.”

Levin went on to provide his followers with even further apparently fascinating details, noting that he’s only kept his AOL email for this long “out of convenience” and now sees “no reason” to continue doing so — and vowing to “address” this apparently riveting saga on his radio show.

The reactions revealed anything but interest, however, even from fellow MAGA supporters.

“Probably an issue with your dial up connection,” wrote Daily Wire commentator Matt Walsh. “Was someone using the landline when you were trying to access the internet? Have you asked anyone on your Buddy List if they’re having similar issues?”

The Blaze columnist Auron MacIntyre went even further and wrote, “The man responsible for advising Trump and propagandizing your parents into supporting a disastrous war is crying about being locked out of his AOL email like it’s 1998.”

Levin was boosted on social media earlier this year by President Donald Trump as “a truly Great American Patriot.” Levin has been a staunch supporter of the Iran war, sparking public rifts between MAGA’s “America First” wing of isolationists and neocon war hawks like himself.

Conservative pundits such as Tucker Carlson and Megyn Kelly have argued Levin’s stance is damaging to America, and English broadcaster Piers Morgan last week called him “the very worst type of permanently enraged, war-mongering imbeciles” after a public feud.

While many social media critics mocked the right-wing commentator over his awkward email saga, Levin was also skewered for more political reasons by voices on both sides of the aisle — who have tired of his pro-war stance and support for Israel amid its ongoing devastation in Gaza.
